title: Dropped or fired: which lands first?
hook: One ball drops off a cliff, one shoots out sideways. Does the fast one stay up longer?

knows: a ball can be thrown sideways
metres, seconds and speeds in m/s
doesNotKnow: that horizontal and vertical motion are independent
the equation y = h - g t^2 / 2

misconception: A ball fired sideways stays up longer, or keeps going straight until its forward push is used up and only then drops.
objective: The learner can explain that, without air drag, a ball's sideways speed changes where it lands but not how long it takes to fall, because gravity acts only vertically.

claims.text: Without air drag, a ball's fall depends only on gravity and the height, not on its sideways speed: both balls are at the same height at every instant.
claims.source: Newton's second law with the only force m g acting vertically: x'' = 0 and y'' = -g, so y(t) = h - g t^2 / 2 for any horizontal speed. Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 4 (Projectile Motion).

claims.text: From 20 m, both balls land 2.02 s after release (g = 9.81 m/s^2).
claims.source: t = sqrt(2 h / g) = sqrt(40 / 9.81) = 2.019 s. Checked by numerical integration of y'' = -g (dt = 1e-5 s): 2.019 s.

claims.text: Fired at 15 m/s, the ball lands 30.3 m from the foot of the cliff; the landing distance is speed times 2.02 s (10.1, 20.2, 30.3, 40.4, 50.5 m for 5 to 25 m/s).
The lesson ignores air drag; with drag the fast ball would be slowed a little and its flight would differ slightly.
claims.source: Stated idealisation. Drag force 1/2 rho C_d A v^2 has a vertical component that depends on total speed, so with drag the motions are no longer independent (Taylor, Classical Mechanics, ch. 2).

claims.text: Gravity pulls only downwards, so it changes the vertical motion and leaves the sideways motion alone.
claims.source: Weight is the vector (0, -m g); its horizontal component is zero, so horizontal velocity is constant. Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 4.

recall.question: A bullet is fired level from a rifle while another bullet is dropped from the same height at the same moment. Ignoring air, which hits the flat ground first?
options: They land at the same time
recall.why: Sideways speed does not change the fall: gravity acts only downwards, so both fall the same height in the same time.
